Identity.History: The Kingdom of Kush flourished along the Nile south of Egypt, with major centers at Napata and later Meroë. Kushite rulers once conquered Egypt and established the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty, while later kings and queens maintained a powerful independent state centered on trade, agriculture, ironworking, and long-distance commerce. Kush repeatedly confronted Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt before declining in the centuries leading to its fall and absorption by the rising kingdom of Aksum.
